sourcedFrom: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1)
cleanIntro: The Mark XXII with the detachable magazine is a .22 LR autoloader whose barrel and receiver come out of the stock as one assembly, held in by a single takedown pin at the rear of the receiver. Weatherby's sheet takes it that far and no further: magazine out, chamber emptied with the shot selector, the pin pushed out, the action lifted from the stock. The hammer, trigger and selector assemblies stay together; they are cleaned where they sit, never taken apart.

steps.title: Safety on: pulled back so the S shows
steps.action: The safety sits on top of the tang, where your thumb reaches it. Pull it back until the S is exposed. That is SAFE; pushed forward to cover the S, the rifle can fire.
steps.prose: Finger outside the trigger guard and the muzzle pointed somewhere safe for everything that follows.
steps.quote: is located conveniently on top of the tang
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — SAFETY, PDF p.2

steps.title: Magazine out: button (G) behind the magazine
steps.action: Press the magazine release button just to the rear of the magazine and take the magazine out of the rifle.
steps.prose: Put it somewhere you can see it. Rounds left in it are still rounds; the rifle is not clear until the chamber is too.
steps.quote: Remove magazine by pressing button (G) to the rear of the magazine.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — LOADING, PDF p.2

steps.title: Selector on SS, operating handle pulled back
steps.action: Set the shot selector, just behind the operating handle on the right side, to SS. Then pull the operating handle back to extract the cartridge from the chamber.
steps.prose: On SS the bolt stays open after it is worked, which is what you want here. Catch the cartridge as it comes out and count it.
steps.quote: and pull back operating handle to extract cartridge from chamber.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — UNLOADING, PDF p.2

steps.title: Bolt left open - look into the chamber
steps.action: Leave the bolt open. Look into the chamber and the magazine well and confirm both are empty.
steps.prose: A look, not an assumption. The sheet says it plainly at the top of its disassembly section: be sure the rifle is unloaded.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — UNLOADING, PDF p.2

steps.title: Takedown pin out, pushed from right to left
steps.action: The takedown pin is at the rear of the receiver. Push it out from the right side toward the left and take it out.
steps.prose: It goes back in from the left, so note which way it came out. Keep it with the magazine.
steps.quote: Remove takedown pin (B) at rear of receiver
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.2

steps.title: Receiver pressed forward, barrel lifted out of the stock
steps.action: With one hand press forward on the receiver, and at the same time lift the barrel carefully with the other. The barrel and receiver come out of the stock together.
steps.prose: Lift, do not pry. If it will not come, check the takedown pin is fully out.
steps.quote: With one hand, press forward on receiver, at the same time carefully lift barrel with the other hand.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.2

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel and receiver assembly is out of the stock, with the magazine and takedown pin beside it. The sheet stops here.
steps.prose: The sheet says no further disassembly is necessary or recommended. The hammer, trigger and selector assemblies stay as they are.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the hammer, trigger and selector assemblies should only be performed by a competent gunsmith or our factory.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.2

steps.title: Bore from the muzzle: solvent, dry patch, oiled patch
steps.action: With the bolt open, put the cleaning rod in from the muzzle and run a bristle brush or a cloth patch wet with powder solvent through the bore. Follow with a dry patch, then a lightly oiled patch.
steps.prose: The sheet cleans this bore from the muzzle. Go gently at the crown.
steps.quote: Insert cleaning rod from muzzle and use bristle brush or cloth patch saturated with powder solvent; follow with dry patch and lightly oiled patch.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — TO CLEAN BORE, PDF p.2

steps.title: Bolt face: solvent, dry cloth, a slightly oiled cloth
steps.action: Clean the face of the bolt with a brush or cloth wet with powder solvent, then a dry cloth, then a slightly oiled cloth.
steps.prose: A slightly oiled cloth means slightly. Oil that pools in an autoloader's action holds the fouling the sheet warns about.
steps.quote: Clean face of bolt with brush or cloth saturated with powder solvent followed by dry cloth, then slightly oiled cloth
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — TO CLEAN BOLT, PDF p.2

steps.title: Underside of the bolt, receiver recess, hammer and selector
steps.action: With the action out of the stock, clean the underside of the bolt and the receiver recess, and the hammer and selector assemblies where they sit.
steps.prose: Clean them in place. They do not come apart on the bench.
steps.quote: The underside of the bolt and receiver recess may be cleaned as well as the hammer and selector assemblies.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.2

steps.title: Metal wiped with a lightly oiled cloth, stock with silicone
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the metal parts with a lightly oiled cloth or a silicone cloth. Wipe the stock with a silicone cloth.
steps.prose: Last, so your hands leave nothing on the finish.
steps.quote: Wipe exterior of metal parts with lightly oiled cloth or silicone cloth.
steps.cite: THE WEATHERBY MARK XXII — Undated two-page instruction sheet with parts list (South Gate, Calif. and Canadian Sauer, Ltd., Toronto addresses on p.1) — TO CLEAN BOLT, PDF p.2

deepAbsentReason: The Mark XXII sheet ends at field disassembly. With the barrel and receiver out of the stock it says no further disassembly is necessary or recommended, and that the hammer, trigger and selector assemblies are taken apart only by a competent gunsmith or Weatherby's factory (PDF p.2). Everything the sheet publishes is in this guide; there is no deeper procedure to follow.

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Bolt open, rod in from the muzzle
Bristle brush or patch wet with powder solvent

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Bolt face: solvent, then a dry cloth, then a slightly oiled cloth
Underside of the bolt and the receiver recess cleaned
Hammer and selector assemblies cleaned where they sit
⛔ Hammer, trigger and selector assemblies are not taken apart

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STOCK
tasks: Outside of the metal: lightly oiled cloth or silicone cloth

reassembly: No ammunition on the bench. Magazine stays out.
Barrel and receiver: set them carefully into the stock and slide them rearward until the holes in the receiver line up.
Takedown pin: insert it at the left side of the rear of the receiver and press it in.
fncheck: The sheet publishes no separate function check. Magazine out, chamber proved empty, muzzle in a safe direction. Pull the safety back so the S shows, then push it forward to cover the S, and back to SAFE: it should move cleanly between the two. With the shot selector on SS, pull the operating handle back: the bolt should stay open; pushing the selector forward should close it. If anything binds, or the takedown pin will not seat flush, stop and take the rifle to a competent gunsmith or Weatherby.
